ANNOUNCEMENTS
Ezekiel Centeno
- World Flying Disk Federation 2026 World Junior Ultimate
Championship
Mayor Hurley congratulated Ezekiel Centeno, Burnaby student, who competed with
Team Canada, and won the World Flying Disk Federation (WFDF) World Junior Ultimate
Championship. The following were the Mayor's remarks:
“Earlier this summer, Burnaby’s own Ezekiel Centeno traveled to Spain to compete with
Team Canada in the WFDF World Junior Ultimate Championships.
Ezekiel, who graduated high school this year, had been the captain of the Vancouver
Christian School ultimate team. He led his team to an unprecedented undefeated
season, and helped them capture the BC School Sports Provincial title for the first time
in school history. But he wasn’t finished there.
As a member of Team Canada, Ezekiel’s play helped propel our national team to the
final against Team USA. And for the first time in 12 years, Canada earned the victory,
capturing the world title.
It’s an incredible achievement that is worth celebrating.
Ezekiel, congratulations on your incredible season, we look forward to cheering you on
for years fo come. Thank you for representing Burnaby with such distinction on the
international stage! Best of luck for the year ahead!"
Simon Fraser University Pipe Band
- 2026 World Pipe Band Championship
Mayor Hurley congratulated the Simon Fraser University Pipe Band on winning the
2026 World Pipe Band Championship. The following were the Mayor's remarks: 

Open Council Meeting
Minutes August 25, 2026
"{ would like to take
a moment to recognize and congratulate the Simon Fraser
University Pipe Band on winning the 2026 World Pipe Band Championships in Glasgow.
This is an incredible achievement, one that speaks to the dedication and talent of the
group. SFU competed against 211 bands from 14 countries
— and they came out on top.
It’s the first win by a Canadian team in 17 years. And the last Canadian team to win was
none other than the SFU Pipe Band.
It’s the seventh title for the band, which includes pipers and drummers from Burnaby,
New Westminster and the Tri-Cities. It’s a great example of the talent SFU helps foster
right here in Burnaby.
The university plays such an important role in our city, from our local economy and
community planning to public safety. SFU reflects Burnaby’s inclusive spirit, creating
opportunities for people across our community. We are so proud of you and this
wonderful achievement. Congratulations!"

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby fee changes to take effect January 1, 2027
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider amendments to the Burnaby Consolidated Fees and Charges Bylaw. A proposed bylaw change would update various municipal fees and charges, with the new rates slated to take effect on January 1, 2027. The specific fees affected have not yet been detailed in the agenda item, but any business that pays municipal fees for licences, permits, or services in Burnaby could be impacted. Council will vote on this proposal at an upcoming meeting.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and review the detailed fee schedule once published to see if your business's fees will change.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to weigh comment on Surrey Metro 2050 amendment
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider sending a comment letter to the Metro Vancouver Regional District Board about a proposed amendment to the Metro 2050 Regional Growth Strategy. The amendment, Bylaw No. 1463, 2026, would change the regional growth plan for a site at 105-175A Street in Surrey. This is a proposed change that has not been approved yet. If you operate in the region, this could affect future planning and development patterns, though the direct impact on Burnaby businesses is still being reviewed.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider forwarding a comment letter to the Metro Vancouver Regional District Board about Amendment Bylaw No. 1470, 2026. This proposed bylaw would amend the Metro 2050 Regional Growth Strategy to change how the Molson Site in Vancouver is planned for future growth. If approved, the amendment could affect regional land-use planning and development patterns that may impact Burnaby businesses. Council will decide whether to submit comments on this proposed change.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to vote on Swangard Stadium LED lighting contract
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to vote on awarding a construction contract for the LED lighting upgrade at Swangard Stadium.
